title: A Compass for the Atlas
premise: In 1847, apprentice clockmaker Jude Galloway is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock, where he discovers the mechanism has been deliberately sabotaged — and that his late father, once the observatory's keeper, may have been involved. When census taker Miriam Ashe begins asking questions about a family that officially never existed, Jude realizes his mother and sister are living under false names to escape a scandal tied to his father's final voyage. As winter closes in and the river ice threatens to trap them forever, Jude must decide who gets the last berth on the spring ferry: the sister who remembers their father as a hero, or the truth-telling mother whose testimony could clear his name but doom them all. He chooses neither — forging a third path by restoring the clock's hidden compartment, which holds proof of his father's innocence, trading his own anonymity for his family's future.
about_author: Casper Brightwater is the pen name of a former horologist's assistant who spent a decade restoring municipal clocks across the river towns of the American Midwest. Their fiction blends mechanical precision with quiet human drama, exploring how ordinary people keep time against history.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Jude Galloway arrives at the observatory to repair its dying master clock, keeping his head down and hands busy. Census taker Miriam Ashe interviews him for the town rolls, then asks about 'the other Galloways' — a family he insists doesn't exist. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine, the first crack in his careful anonymity.

chapters.title: Escapement
chapters.summary: Inside the clock's works, Jude finds evidence of deliberate sabotage: a filed tooth, a misaligned pallet, work done by someone skilled. His father taught him these very mechanisms before vanishing on a river expedition years ago. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: dawning suspicion that the past he buried is ticking back toward him.

chapters.title: The House on Ferry Lane
chapters.summary: Jude visits his mother Ruth and sister Ada, who live under the surname Hale. Ada idolizes their father; Ruth refuses to speak of him at all. That night, Miriam Ashe knocks on their door with her census book open. POV: alternating Jude and Ruth. Emotional beat: the fragile architecture of a family built on silence beginning to groan.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Kept
chapters.summary: Ruth confesses part of it: Jude's father was accused of stealing expedition funds before his disappearance, and the family changed names to survive the shame. She believes he was guilty; Ada cannot bear to hear it. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth made flesh — a mother choosing a livable lie over a devastating truth.

chapters.title: Miriam's Book
chapters.summary: Miriam Ashe reveals she isn't merely taking a census — she's investigating the old expedition scandal for a magistrate reopening the case, and the missing Galloways are her last loose thread. She offers Jude a bargain: cooperate, and his family avoids prosecution for falsified records. POV: Miriam. Emotional beat: sympathy entangled with threat; an antagonist who believes she is right.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: The river freezes early and hard. The ferry company announces one final berth will be sold before full ice-out — passage for exactly one person, guaranteed departure before the magistrate's summons can be served. Ruth insists Ada take it; Ada refuses to leave without their father's name cleared. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing as literally as the river.

chapters.title: The Hidden Compartment
chapters.summary: Working feverishly on the master clock, Jude discovers a sealed chamber behind the chime barrel — his father's design. Inside: a ledger proving the funds were taken by the expedition's patron, not his father, along with a letter begging forgiveness. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: grief and vindication colliding; the father he mourned returns as a stranger worth defending.

chapters.title: A Thief's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Jude brings the ledger to Miriam, but she warns him the magistrate cares more about closing files than justice — and the patron's family still holds power. The berth deadline arrives. Ruth secretly buys it for herself, planning to surrender and spare her children. POV: Jude and Ada. Emotional beat: love against duty, each family member sacrificing alone instead of together.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: At the frozen dock, Jude stops the ferry. He gives the berth to Ada — not to flee, but to carry the ledger to the magistrate in the capital, the only route around the compromised local court. He publicly claims the Galloway name before the whole town. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: climax — the choice made, identity surrendered, no way back.

chapters.title: Keeping Time
chapters.summary: Spring breaks the ice. The magistrate exonerates Jude's father posthumously; Ruth weeps at the restored name on the expedition memorial. Jude finishes repairing the master clock and sets it running true, staying in the town that now knows him. POV: Jude. Emotional beat: resolution — memory honored, truth survived, and a man finally at home in his own time.
